Drop Longhorn: cutover to local-nvme + NFS backups (PR 2 of 2) (#324)

* Drop Longhorn: flip stateful charts to local-nvme + wire backup CronJobs (PR 2 of 2)

PR1 (#321) scaffolded the infrastructure (local-storage chart with static
local-nvme PVs, k8s_data_dirs role, backups chart with NFS CronJobs, NAS
runbook). This PR is the cutover: chart StorageClass flips, NFS path
migration, Longhorn removal, and decommission surgery.

Chart cutover:
- supabase.yaml, grafana.yaml, open-webui.yaml: storageClassName longhorn
  -> local-nvme across all three persistence blocks + prometheus; removed
  redundant NotIn ws03 nodeAffinity blocks (local PV nodeAffinity is a
  stronger constraint).
- values.yaml: rkllama/llamacpp/supabase NFS paths migrated to the single
  managed /bigdisk/k8s-cluster/* subtree; added top-level nfs block for
  the backups chart to consume.
- New kubernetes-services/templates/backups.yaml ArgoCD Application.

Longhorn removal:
- Deleted templates/longhorn.yaml and additions/longhorn/.
- argo-project.yaml: dropped charts.longhorn.io from sourceRepos.
- roles/cluster/vars/main.yml: removed vestigial cluster_longhorn_*.
- roles/tools/tasks/scripts.yml: removed Longhorn connection script.
- roles/update_packages: dropped open-iscsi (kept nfs-common).

Decommission surgery (pb_decommission.yml):
- Removed ~150 lines of Longhorn teardown (volume detach wait, finalizer
  stripping, CRD cleanup, iSCSI logout, /var/lib/longhorn wipe).
- Kept the scale-down + PVC-delete loop (still needed so chart-owned
  PVCs re-create cleanly on next sync and re-bind to the preserved PVs).
- Added backups to the namespace delete list.
- Added new gated 'wipe_local_data' task: /home/k8s-data and
  /var/lib/k8s-data are PRESERVED by default; pass -e wipe_local_data=true
  only for a genuine clean-slate rebuild.

Meta:
- .claude/commands/rebuild-cluster.md: rewritten DATA LOSS warning
  around the new preservation model, added one-time NAS prereq note.
- CLAUDE.md: two new hard rules (sacred local PV paths; explicit
  host-pinning for new local-nvme workloads).
- PLAN.md: storage table/diagram updated.

Docs:
- docs/how-to/backup-restore.md: rewritten around CronJob schedule +
  Postgres/tar/sqlite restore recipes.
- docs/how-to/alternative-storage.md: describes static-local + NFS-backup
  as the default; Longhorn is now one of several replacement options.
- docs/explanations/kubernetes-services.md: new "Storage layer" section
  covering local-storage and backups charts.
- New ADR 0012 captures rationale and rejected alternatives.
- ADR 0009 (Longhorn workstation exclusion) marked superseded.

Out of scope for this PR (to keep blast radius minimal):
- ~25 narrative docs and commands that still mention Longhorn in prose
  (home landing page card, test-oauth-flow matrix, various
  docs/explanations and docs/reference pages). Follow-up cleanup PR.

Post-merge note: merging this PR does NOT immediately swap the live
PVCs off Longhorn -- storageClassName on existing PVCs is immutable.
ArgoCD will show OutOfSync on supabase/grafana/open-webui until
/rebuild-cluster re-creates them. The supabase-db backup CronJob
starts working at 02:00 the first night; the other four rely on
hostPath volumes under /home/k8s-data and /var/lib/k8s-data, which
don't exist on the nodes until k8s_data_dirs runs, so they will
CreateContainerError nightly until the user runs
'ansible-playbook pb_all.yml --tags servers' or kicks off
/rebuild-cluster.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Re-seal all secrets for rebuilt cluster

* Fix: seal supabase-credentials into backups namespace for pg_dump cronjobs

The supabase-db-daily/weekly CronJobs run in the backups namespace (to
mount the k8s-cluster-nfs PVC directly) but reference supabase-credentials
via secretKeyRef. The secret was only sealed into the supabase namespace,
so pg_dump pods failed with CreateContainerConfigError / secret not found.

Seal the same values into the backups namespace too and wire it into
seal-from-json so future rebuilds keep them in sync. Discovered during
/rebuild-cluster validation of PR #324 (drop-Longhorn cutover).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs: add ADR 0012 to toctree and fix backup-restore xref

Two sphinx warnings that fail the docs CI job (warnings treated as
errors):

1. docs/explanations/decisions/0012-drop-longhorn.md is not referenced
   from docs/explanations/decisions.md toctree, so it never gets built
   into the site.

2. The {doc} cross-reference `../how-to/backup-restore` resolves to
   `explanations/how-to/backup-restore` (wrong); correct path is
   `../../how-to/backup-restore`.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

@@ -0,0 +1,161 @@
+# 12. Drop Longhorn in Favour of Static Local PVs + NFS Backups
+
+**Status:** Accepted
+
+**Supersedes:** 0009 (workstation exclusion from Longhorn — no longer
+relevant with Longhorn removed).
+
+## Context
+
+The cluster previously used Longhorn as its block-storage CSI provider for
+six stateful PVCs (Supabase `db`/`storage`/`minio`, Grafana, Prometheus,
+Open WebUI), totalling about 225Gi of live data. Two compounding problems
+forced a rethink:
+
+1. **`/rebuild-cluster` destroys all Longhorn data.** The decommission
+   playbook wipes `/var/lib/longhorn` and `/var/lib/rancher`, and Longhorn's
+   volume metadata lives in Kubernetes CRDs that are gone once the cluster
+   is torn down. Every rebuild was therefore a total loss of Supabase,
+   Grafana history, and Open WebUI chat state.
+2. **No backup system.** Longhorn's built-in volume snapshots are
+   node-local and vanish with the node. Longhorn-to-NFS backup targets
+   exist but were never wired up, because the recovery story still
+   required a Longhorn cluster on the other side.
+
+Additionally, the RK1 nodes each have a 1TB NVMe sitting mostly unused
+(OS + free space) and nuc2 has a 931GB `/home` disk mounted at `/home`,
+so local high-quality storage is already paid for.
+
+The NAS (`gknas`, `192.168.1.3`) hosts existing NFS shares for LLM models
+(rkllama/llamacpp) and Supabase DB dumps, *plus unrelated personal shares*
+(JellyFin library, files, etc.) that must not be touched. Any NAS change
+has to respect that trust boundary.
+
+## Decision
+
+**Drop Longhorn entirely. Replace it with two orthogonal layers:**
+
+1. **Per-node static local PVs** (`additions/local-storage/`). A
+   `local-nvme` `StorageClass` with `provisioner: kubernetes.io/no-provisioner`,
+   `volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer`, and `reclaimPolicy: Retain`.
+   Six static `PersistentVolume` objects — one per live Longhorn PVC —
+   each pre-bound via `spec.claimRef: {namespace, name}` to the exact
+   chart-generated PVC name, and pinned via `spec.nodeAffinity` to a
+   specific node:
+
+   | PVC | Node | On-disk path |
+   |-----|------|---|
+   | `supabase-db` | nuc2 | `/home/k8s-data/supabase-db` |
+   | `supabase-storage` | nuc2 | `/home/k8s-data/supabase-storage` |
+   | `supabase-minio` | nuc2 | `/home/k8s-data/supabase-minio` |
+   | `storage-grafana-prometheus-0` | node03 | `/var/lib/k8s-data/grafana` |
+   | `prometheus-grafana-prometheus-kube-pr-prometheus-...` | node02 | `/var/lib/k8s-data/prometheus` |
+   | `open-webui` | node04 | `/var/lib/k8s-data/open-webui` |
+
+   The `k8s_data_dirs` Ansible role creates these directories
+   idempotently (part of the `servers` play), with owner/mode chosen to
+   match each workload's pod `securityContext`. `pb_decommission.yml`
+   **preserves** `/home/k8s-data` and `/var/lib/k8s-data` by default; a
+   new opt-in flag `-e wipe_local_data=true` removes them for a genuine
+   clean-slate rebuild.
+
+2. **Per-app backup CronJobs writing to one NFS share on the NAS**
+   (`additions/backups/`). A single cluster-owned subtree
+   `/bigdisk/k8s-cluster/` hosts all cluster data the cluster reads or
+   writes over NFS — LLM models, Supabase DB dumps, and the new backup
+   targets (`backups/<app>/{,weekly}`). One static NFS `PV`/`PVC` covers
+   the whole subtree; each CronJob mounts it with a workload-specific
+   `subPath`. Daily + weekly schedules per app; retention is enforced
+   in-job with `find -mtime`. Prometheus is deliberately excluded —
+   metrics are reconstructible from re-scrape.
+
+## Rejected alternatives
+
+### Keep Longhorn, add a backup pipeline
+
+Possible, but doesn't fix the fundamental problem: a rebuild destroys the
+primary data store and the restore path would need a working Longhorn
+cluster on the other side. Longhorn is also the single biggest source of

+significantly.

+
+`local-path-provisioner` is already the default StorageClass (bundled
+with k3s), so in principle we could just point charts at it. Rejected
+because its PVC→`hostPath` bindings live in **etcd** — they are lost
+when the cluster is rebuilt. The new cluster's `local-path-provisioner`
+would allocate a brand new `hostPath` for each PVC, not re-bind to the
+existing on-disk data. Static PVs with `claimRef` pinning are the only
+way to guarantee a PVC re-binds to the *same* directory after a rebuild.

+access to it would require a trust boundary we don't want, and QTS

+Ansible-written configuration would be fragile. Decision: **NAS setup

+Supabase runs its init migrations fresh, Grafana starts with empty
+dashboards (we had no saved dashboards), Prometheus starts empty (fine),
+Open WebUI starts empty (chat history was disposable). A one-time
+fresh-start cost was deemed acceptable versus the effort of tar-dumping
+Longhorn volumes and restoring them into raw hostPath directories with
+the right ownership.

+  same dashboards, Open WebUI shows the same chat history.
